behavior: In History with a copy job in flight the footer reads 'Esc Cancel copy' and omits 'y Copy' at widths 40, 80 and 120; the first Esc cancels the job (Redraw), the second leaves History; Copy mode's footer names COPY, Esc Back, v Select and y Copy.
failure_caught: A footer that still advertises 'y Copy' while a job is running, or an Esc that returns to Browse and drops the pending selection instead of cancelling the job.
criticality_reason: Only footer wording/affordance changes here; the copy data path is untouched (keymap.rs:800-825).
signal_reason: Asserts positive and negative substrings at three widths plus the two-step Esc state transition (state.rs:2384-2400).
uniqueness_reason: The non-copy footer wording is already protected by the built-in dashboard footer test; this adds only the Cancel-copy/-job state distinction.
fidelity_reason: Renders the real Dashboard through TestBackend; no stand-in for the footer.
recommendation_reason: Distinct cancel-copy affordance and Esc ordering not covered by the retained footer test.

behavior: In Copy mode a left-drag from a wide CJK cell to the next cell makes y emit '界z'; clicking the drawn copy control repeats the same text; clicking the close control exits Copy so q detaches.
failure_caught: Dragging onto a wide-cell continuation and copying a half-glyph or empty selection, or copy/close hitboxes targeting the wrong control.
criticality_reason: Wrong copied text is a bounded copy-feature failure, not durable state loss.
signal_reason: Asserts the exact copied string, the control-driven copy action and the post-close detach transition.
uniqueness_reason: Wide-cell mouse normalization is a distinct boundary from the built-in keyboard wide-cell copy test.
fidelity_reason: Real Dashboard + production CopySelection/control geometry; clipboard writing is outside this state boundary.
recommendation_reason: Protects wide-cell mouse selection and the copy/close controls end to end.

behavior: A drag in frozen History maps screen cells through the viewport's top/left offsets and emits a HistoryPage; the copy control then shows 'copying' while the job needs pages; a new press in the pane cancels the in-flight job and close+q detach.
failure_caught: Offsets applied twice or not at all so the anchor lands on a different row, or a stale page completion rendering after the gesture was cancelled.
criticality_reason: A wrong frozen range copies the wrong text; bounded copy failure.
signal_reason: Positive/negative 'copying' assertions bracket the cancel transition, with page requests pumped through the real frozen history.
uniqueness_reason: Frozen-offset mouse mapping and stale-completion cancellation are distinct from other copy/history tests.
fidelity_reason: Uses a real FrozenHistory capture and the real Dashboard page pipeline.
recommendation_reason: Covers offset mapping plus the stale page completion/cancel boundary.

behavior: Release at a cell fixes the endpoint ('abc'); a later drag without a press does not extend it; FocusLost finishes the gesture so a drag after focus regain starts from the new press and y yields 'b'.
failure_caught: Drag events after release or across focus loss silently extending the selection, so copied text is larger than the visible selection.
criticality_reason: Wrong selection bounds are a bounded copy failure.
signal_reason: Exact copied strings before and after release/focus-loss transitions, including the negative post-release drag.
uniqueness_reason: Focus-loss bounding of a copy gesture is a distinct failure boundary.
fidelity_reason: Real Dashboard, real event dispatch and selection code.
recommendation_reason: Protects gesture lifetime against release position and focus loss.

behavior: Opening which-key with '?' during a Copy or History mouse drag ends the gesture: the following Up/Drag select nothing, Esc+y in Copy yields only 'a', and History stays in History with no PTY bytes.
failure_caught: A gesture that keeps tracking under the overlay, so a drag after which-key closes extends a stale anchor.
criticality_reason: Wrong selection extension is a bounded copy failure.
signal_reason: Asserts exact retained selection in Copy and HISTORY footer plus no-PtyBytes for the History yank.
uniqueness_reason: Overlay acquisition cancelling a capture gesture is a distinct integration boundary.
fidelity_reason: Real Dashboard with both real gestures and the real which-key overlay.
recommendation_reason: Only coverage of overlay acquisition clearing an in-progress capture drag.

behavior: A press on a painted cell then release elsewhere requests only HistoryPage messages and y while pages are missing stays Redraw; presses above/below the pane return None; resize keeps the frozen HISTORY view and a focus change drops it.
failure_caught: A click on unpainted space creating an anchor, or resize/focus invalidation keeping or dropping the frozen capture at the wrong time.
criticality_reason: Wrong anchor/invalidated capture is a bounded history-copy failure.
signal_reason: Exact outbox-type assertion, None for out-of-pane presses and the resize/focus negative transition.
uniqueness_reason: Painted-cell bounds and resize capture retention are distinct from other history tests.
fidelity_reason: Real pane geometry, real page pipeline and render checks.
recommendation_reason: Protects painted-cell hit-testing and capture lifetime across resize/focus.

behavior: A History copy across a row marked wrapped joins the text without inserting a hard newline (keeping the wide glyph); when a page is still needed it emits another HistoryPage instead.
failure_caught: HistoryCopyJob::consume_page inserting '\n' at a wrapped row boundary or splitting a wide cell, producing text different from what the terminal displayed.
criticality_reason: Corrupted copied text is a bounded copy failure.
signal_reason: On the CopyText branch it checks the wide glyph and the absence of '界\n', but it accepts a Redraw/HistoryPage branch as a pass, so a copy that never completes escapes.
uniqueness_reason: The built-in soft-wrap test covers CopySelection::selected_text, not the History page job's wrapped-row newline rule.
fidelity_reason: Real History page job through the Dashboard, with the job's own wrapped metadata.
recommendation_reason: Distinct wrapped-row rule in HistoryCopyJob; the permissive second branch limits signal.

behavior: PageUp over an alternate-screen program requests a Transcript and opens a read-only modal that escapes control sequences, swallows keys/paste/mouse/Ctrl-o, keeps its original entries when the page identity changes, closes on run change, leaves a muted footer when no transcript exists, stays quiet for a cancelled begin or plain wheel, and still errors on other failures.
failure_caught: PageUp writing to the agent PTY or surfacing a raw Conflict; provider escape sequences reaching the terminal; a wrong-conversation page replacing the view; a cancelled open still taking the screen.
criticality_reason: Transcript access is a bounded feature; failure loses a read-only view but no durable state.
signal_reason: Multiple precise positive/negative assertions across request identity, modal input isolation, escaped controls, muted-limit and error branches.
uniqueness_reason: The open/modal/identity path is unique; only the no-transcript muted/quiet sub-cases are also covered by retained coverage.
fidelity_reason: Real Dashboard rendering with protocol fixtures; transcript retrieval itself is a server fixture, which is appropriate for the TUI boundary.
recommendation_reason: Broad but decisive protection of the transcript modal's inputs, rendering and lifecycle.

behavior: Esc while the transcript's first page is in flight closes the modal; a late Transcript response then renders neither the modal nor its entries.
failure_caught: A stale opening response re-opening an empty modal or leaking provider text after the user closed it.
criticality_reason: A stale read-only modal is a bounded UI failure.
signal_reason: Asserts both the absence of the Transcript title and of the late entry text after the close.
uniqueness_reason: This stale-open-after-close transition is not covered by the main transcript test.
fidelity_reason: Real Dashboard, real response routing and render.
recommendation_reason: Only test of the pending-open cancellation plus late-page drop.

behavior: Home asks for an older page, End immediately issues a distinct newest-page request; the older response is discarded (its text never appears) while the tail stays, and the newest response replaces the older content.
failure_caught: Request-id reuse or End being suppressed while a page is pending, letting the older page append after the user asked for the newest.
criticality_reason: Wrong transcript paging shows stale conversation content; bounded view failure.
signal_reason: Asserts distinct request ids, exact newest request shape, stale-page non-render and replacement of entry-0 by the newest text.
uniqueness_reason: Superseding a pending older request with End is a distinct request-lifecycle boundary.
fidelity_reason: Real Dashboard request/response pipeline and render.
recommendation_reason: Protects request supersession and newest-page replacement.

behavior: After 9000-entry pages are loaded and another 9000-entry older page arrives, the view remains a bounded window ('Bounded window' note) and asks for before=42 then before=21; End issues a fresh newest request and clears the note.
failure_caught: Unbounded growth beyond the entry cap, paging from the wrong offset, or End leaving the truncated window state.
criticality_reason: Unbounded transcript memory or wrong paging is a bounded feature failure.
signal_reason: Exact before offsets, the window note assertion and its disappearance after End replace.
uniqueness_reason: The bounded-window accounting across prepends is distinct from the plain paging test.
fidelity_reason: Real Dashboard with real trim_view/row_count; transcript data is a fixture.
recommendation_reason: Only coverage of the truncation/window boundary sequence.

behavior: A single assistant entry with 70,001 logical lines renders 'transcript-tail-marker' in a 120x40 viewport.
failure_caught: Ratatui's u16 Paragraph scroll offset truncating a >65535 visual-row offset, so the painted window shows a middle region and the true tail is invisible.
criticality_reason: A clipped read-only transcript is a bounded feature failure.
signal_reason: One decisive invariant (tail marker visible) that fails for any offset truncation; the fixture forces the >u16 condition.
uniqueness_reason: No other test exercises the >u16 scroll-offset path; scrollable_lines is only evidenced here.
fidelity_reason: Real Dashboard transcript render through TestBackend; the offset computation is production code.
recommendation_reason: Only decisive coverage of the u16 scroll-offset guard.

behavior: p emits PauseSession; a Conflict response for that request puts the message in the footer behind 'ERROR:' rather than the muted limit form.
failure_caught: Classifying the Server's Conflict for a real pause signal failure as an expected limit, so a failed pause looks like a benign wait.
criticality_reason: A mislabeled but visible failure is a bounded workflow/feedback problem.
signal_reason: Asserts the exact footer string including the ERROR: marker for the Conflict code path.
uniqueness_reason: The pause request path is distinct input within the same error-classification contract covered by the recovery and resume cases.
fidelity_reason: Real request emission and real response routing through the Dashboard.
recommendation_reason: Specific Conflict-must-be-an-error boundary for pause.

behavior: A Conflict response to Request::Input shows the plain message with no ERROR: marker, while an Internal response to a later Input shows 'ERROR: write to pty: broken pipe'.
failure_caught: Treating input admission refusals as fatal errors, or a genuine PTY write failure as a benign limit.
criticality_reason: Feedback classification only; input already failed, so consequence is bounded.
signal_reason: Asserts both sides of the was_input special case with exact footer text.
uniqueness_reason: The input-specific Conflict-to-limit branch is distinct from the general set_server_error matrix.
fidelity_reason: Real Dashboard request/response path; PTY itself is not exercised (server responses are fixtures).
recommendation_reason: Only coverage of the input-admission-limit versus write-failure split.

behavior: In the paused phase r emits ResumeSession; a Conflict response puts 'ERROR: could not continue...' in the footer.
failure_caught: A failed resume being shown as a muted limit, hiding that the session is still paused because the signal failed.
criticality_reason: Bounded lifecycle feedback problem; the session stays paused either way.
signal_reason: Exact footer assertion including the ERROR: marker after the paused-phase transition.
uniqueness_reason: The resume request path is a distinct input within the already-covered error classification contract.
fidelity_reason: Real hierarchy transition, request emission and response routing.
recommendation_reason: Resume-specific Conflict classification; small distinction over the pause case.

behavior: Two wheel-up ticks over frozen History move the header's first row from top to top-3 to top-6, and one tick down returns to top-3.
failure_caught: Wheel ticks moving one row, overshooting, or resetting the viewport so the header row disagrees with the painted cells.
criticality_reason: Wrong scroll step is a bounded history usability failure.
signal_reason: Reads the painted header row before/after and asserts exact arithmetic across three ticks, with frozen pages pumped.
uniqueness_reason: Wheel step size is distinct from the history open-at-tail and leave-at-live wheel tests.
fidelity_reason: Real FrozenHistory pages and real Dashboard wheel dispatch.
recommendation_reason: Exact three-row step protected against off-by-one/clamping regressions.

behavior: The Events popup filters by every whitespace word, case-insensitively, across component/subject/message; events stay oldest-first; Esc clears the filter before it closes the popup.
failure_caught: An OR/whole-string filter that keeps non-matching events, case-sensitive matching, reversed ordering, or Esc closing the popup while a filter is set.
criticality_reason: Wrong event filtering is a bounded feature failure.
signal_reason: Positive and negative event text assertions across two filters, ordering, and the two-stage Esc behavior.
uniqueness_reason: Word-AND semantics and Esc precedence are distinct from component filtering and live append.
fidelity_reason: Real Dashboard popup with real Request::Events response handling and render.
recommendation_reason: Distinct filter semantics and dismissal ordering.

behavior: Tab cycles all→titles→settings→quota, BackTab reverses, the component filter composes with the word filter (No events match.), and BackTab is inert while the word filter is being typed.
failure_caught: Tab/BackTab changing the component during filter editing, wrong cycle direction, or the filters not composing.
criticality_reason: Wrong event filtering is a bounded feature failure.
signal_reason: Asserts each component selection with included/excluded event text and that Enter ends editing before BackTab acts.
uniqueness_reason: Component cycling plus filter-editing gating is distinct from the word filter test.
fidelity_reason: Real Dashboard key handling, filtering and render.
recommendation_reason: Cycle direction and edit-mode gating both protected.

behavior: Events recorded while the popup is open append after the snapshot without asking for the ring again, an event recorded while closed is not shown, and a reopened popup starts fresh from the new snapshot.
failure_caught: Live events dropped or duplicated, a re-request per event, and buffered closed-popup events leaking into the next open.
criticality_reason: A degraded event log is a bounded feature failure.
signal_reason: Asserts absence of a new Events request, ordering of old vs live entries, and that closed-time events never surface.
uniqueness_reason: Live append plus snapshot merge is distinct from the filter tests.
fidelity_reason: Real Dashboard with Recorded events and the real merge path.
recommendation_reason: Only coverage of live append and closed-time event isolation.

behavior: With 40 events the popup opens showing ev-39 (not ev-00), Home shows ev-00 (not ev-39), and End returns to ev-39.
failure_caught: Opening stuck at the oldest event, or Home/End moving the stick/scroll state in the wrong direction.
criticality_reason: Wrong initial scroll hides newest events; bounded usability failure.
signal_reason: Exact include/exclude assertions for the two ends across Home/End.
uniqueness_reason: A simple scroll-stick boundary within the already-covered events contract.
fidelity_reason: Real Dashboard popup and render.
recommendation_reason: Protects open-at-newest and Home/End semantics.

behavior: An Error response for an unknown request id shows 'ERROR: session 99 not found' in the footer and never prints the raw ErrorCode name.
failure_caught: Ordinary errors being swallowed when they match no pending request, or leaking the internal error code instead of plain words.
criticality_reason: Missing error feedback is a bounded diagnostic failure.
signal_reason: One exact positive string and one exact negative string for the NotFound path.
uniqueness_reason: Same footer contract as the classification tests; this adds the unmatched-request fallback case.
fidelity_reason: Real Dashboard response routing and footer render.
recommendation_reason: Small but distinct unmatched-response visibility check.

behavior: encode_key maps Ctrl-g and a raw BEL to Browse, and Ctrl-c to the single byte 0x03.
failure_caught: Ctrl-g being forwarded to the child (dashboard can no longer reserve it) or Ctrl-c failing to reach the program so an agent cannot be interrupted.
criticality_reason: Losing Ctrl-c delivery blocks interrupting a runaway agent; Ctrl-g misrouting also breaks the dashboard escape path.
signal_reason: Exact KeyEncoding variants and byte vectors for three distinct keys.
uniqueness_reason: The Ctrl-g/Ctrl-c reservation is a distinct safety boundary within the broader key-encoding contract.
fidelity_reason: Direct invocation of the full production encode_key wrapper (pure algorithm), so no boundary is faked.
recommendation_reason: High-consequence key reservation with exact encodings.

behavior: encode_paste emits the raw text when bracketed paste is off and wraps it in ESC[200~/ESC[201~ when on.
failure_caught: Missing or duplicated bracketed-paste framing, so a multiline paste is executed line-by-line in the child program.
criticality_reason: Paste framing corruption affects a single paste action; bounded.
signal_reason: Two exact byte-vector assertions cover both modes but no embedded-escape or empty-paste boundary.
uniqueness_reason: The raw encoder contract is almost entirely exercised by the dashboard paste test; only the framing bytes are distinct.
fidelity_reason: Direct production encode_paste invocation (pure encoder).
recommendation_reason: Cheap exact contract check; small distinct boundary over the dashboard path.

behavior: After the focused screen enables bracketed paste and Enter enters Terminal mode, a Paste event becomes PtyBytes wrapped in the bracketed markers.
failure_caught: Paste being dropped, sent unframed while the program enabled bracketed paste, or routed as ordinary keystrokes.
criticality_reason: One paste action goes wrong; bounded feature failure.
signal_reason: Exact PtyBytes assertion for the enabled mode; the disabled mode is only covered by the pure encoder test.
uniqueness_reason: The dashboard routing of a paste event to the focused session is distinct from the encoder test.
fidelity_reason: Real pane screen state, real mode transition and real Dashboard dispatch.
recommendation_reason: Protects paste routing against the pane's bracketed-paste state.

behavior: The dashboard reader channel accepts exactly DASHBOARD_READER_QUEUE_CAPACITY messages and the next try_send returns Full.
failure_caught: The reader channel becoming unbounded (server messages accumulate without bound when the dashboard is slow) or its capacity collapsing so the reader blocks/deadlocks.
criticality_reason: Unbounded buffering threatens responsiveness/memory but has a straightforward restart workaround.
signal_reason: Asserts the exact capacity boundary with Full on the next send, but does not exercise read_messages blocking or the drain loop.
uniqueness_reason: The bounded-queue contract is tested nowhere else; it is a single boundary with no extra transition.
fidelity_reason: Uses the production channel constructor and capacity constant, but the reader thread's blocking send is replaced by a direct try_send.
recommendation_reason: Only protection for the bounded reader queue; cheap and exact at its boundary.

behavior: Output for a newly focused session that has no acknowledged screen is not painted, the previous session's pane content is gone, and after install_screen the new screen and later live output both render.
failure_caught: Applying live output to a stale or different session's pane (wrong-session display), or keeping the previous screen after the selection changed.
criticality_reason: Showing another session's output in the selected pane is a wrong-ownership display that can mislead the user about which agent produced text.
signal_reason: Positive/negative text assertions across before-screen, stale-pane, and post-screen transitions.
uniqueness_reason: The output-before-screen gating is distinct from the ack/burst handshake tests.
fidelity_reason: Real Dashboard pane state, install_screen acknowledgement and render.
recommendation_reason: Protects the screen-before-output ownership boundary.

behavior: Ctrl punctuation (space/@, backslash/4, ]/5, ^/6, _/7) encode to the terminals' control bytes, Ctrl-c keeps 0x03 under every modifier combination, and Shift/Alt/Ctrl arrows, Enter, Backspace and PageUp produce their CSI sequences.
failure_caught: A wrong table entry sending a different control byte or CSI sequence, so programs misinterpret modified keys (e.g. Ctrl-Space vs NUL collisions, Shift-Enter submitted as plain Enter).
criticality_reason: Wrong bytes to a program are a bounded feature failure inside the pane.
signal_reason: A wide exact-byte matrix with independent expected values and a modifier sweep.
uniqueness_reason: Punctuation and modified-key encodings are distinct inputs from the Ctrl-g/Ctrl-c reservation test.
fidelity_reason: Direct full production encode_key invocation (pure encoder).
recommendation_reason: Exact matrix protects the terminal input contract.

behavior: After a stopped→running hierarchy transition the old screen text is gone, the manual title stays, and the emitted SetView binds the pane to the live run.
failure_caught: Keeping a dead run's screen after the session restarts, or reusing the old run id in SetView so input targets a dead run.
criticality_reason: A stale dead-run screen misrepresents ownership of the pane and could receive input intended for the new run.
signal_reason: Asserts absence of old output, presence of the preserved title, and the exact live (session,run) pair in SetView.
uniqueness_reason: Run-change invalidation is distinct from the burst/ack handshake tests.
fidelity_reason: Real Dashboard state machine, real SetView composition and render.
recommendation_reason: Protects run rebinding and stale-screen clearing on restart.

behavior: SGR encoding for down/up (m suffix), middle/right buttons, four wheel directions, drag/motion codes, >223 coordinates and Shift/Alt/Ctrl modifier bits all match the expected byte strings.
failure_caught: Wrong SGR button/release/modifier/coordinate codes, e.g. a release reported as a press or wheel codes off by one, so child programs act on phantom clicks.
criticality_reason: Wrong mouse bytes affect a bounded interaction inside the pane.
signal_reason: Exact byte assertions across every button, release, wheel, motion and modifier combination, including a coordinate beyond the legacy limit.
uniqueness_reason: SGR event encoding is distinct from protocol-mode filtering and legacy-encoding boundary tests.
fidelity_reason: Direct full production encode_mouse invocation (pure encoder).
recommendation_reason: Complete exact SGR matrix.

behavior: Mode filtering: None emits nothing; Press mode emits only presses; PressRelease adds releases but no drag/motion; ButtonMotion emits drags but not motion; AnyMotion emits motion; wheel events are suppressed in x10 Press mode.
failure_caught: Events leaking past the negotiated tracking mode, so a program receives drags/ups/wheels it never requested.
criticality_reason: Wrong tracking mode bytes affect a bounded program interaction.
signal_reason: Full matrix over seven event kinds against four protocol modes, including the negative cases per mode.
uniqueness_reason: Mode filtering is a distinct invariant from event code encoding.
fidelity_reason: Direct full production encode_mouse invocation (pure encoder).
recommendation_reason: Decisive mode-filter matrix.

behavior: Legacy X10 encoding emits ESC[M + offset bytes for (0,0), accepts 222 and rejects 223 for Default, accepts 2014 and rejects 2015 for UTF-8, encodes U+07FF for Utf8, keeps SGR coordinates at u16::MAX, and encodes release as button 3.
failure_caught: Off-by-one limit arithmetic or invalid bytes emitted for coordinates past 223/2015, producing corrupt mouse reports in legacy programs.
criticality_reason: Corrupt legacy mouse reports affect a bounded interaction.
signal_reason: Exact boundary triples at each limit with accept and reject sides.
uniqueness_reason: Legacy/UTF-8 boundary encoding is a distinct input space from SGR encoding.
fidelity_reason: Direct full production encode_mouse invocation (pure encoder).
recommendation_reason: Only coverage of legacy encoding limits.

behavior: A Moved event over the sidebar then enabling any-motion tracking: a Moved event inside the pane is forwarded as PtyBytes and the sidebar row no longer shows a hover marker.
failure_caught: Sidebar hover state swallowing the first pane motion event, or leaving a stale hover marker painted over the sidebar.
criticality_reason: A swallowed/misplaced motion event is a bounded interaction defect.
signal_reason: Asserts PtyBytes forwarding plus a negative render check for the sidebar marker.
uniqueness_reason: Hover-to-pane motion handoff is a distinct boundary from the pure encoding tests.
fidelity_reason: Real Dashboard with real sidebar/pane geometry and render.
recommendation_reason: Protects the sidebar-hover-to-pane transition.

behavior: A Browse-mode click inside the focused pane returns Redraw without PTY bytes, and a following x is encoded as 'x'.
failure_caught: The click also being forwarded to the child (phantom click before the user typed) or the mode not switching to Terminal.
criticality_reason: A phantom click in a child is a bounded misrouting.
signal_reason: Negative assertion on the click action plus a positive typed-byte assertion after focus.
uniqueness_reason: The focus-without-forward rule overlaps the other pane-click tests but adds the already-focused single-pane case.
fidelity_reason: Real Dashboard geometry and dispatch.
recommendation_reason: Small distinct boundary within the pane-click contract.

behavior: Clicking the other pane of a split focuses it; typing before its screen is acknowledged returns Redraw (no bytes), and after install_screen the same key is sent to that session.
failure_caught: Typing after a focus change reaching the previously focused session, or input being accepted before the new pane's screen is known.
criticality_reason: Input delivered to the wrong session is a wrong-target action.
signal_reason: Positive/negative action assertions around the acknowledgement boundary.
uniqueness_reason: Focus-change gating on the view acknowledgement is distinct from mouse forwarding tests.
fidelity_reason: Real split panes, ack handshake and key dispatch.
recommendation_reason: Protects wrong-session typing across pane focus changes.

behavior: In Terminal mode with tracking enabled, clicking the other pane returns Redraw and focuses it, but the click is not forwarded to the previously focused application; typing stays gated.
failure_caught: The pane-switch click being forwarded to the app already focused, delivering a click the user never aimed at it.
criticality_reason: A stray click inside an agent can trigger a destructive UI action in that program; wrong-target input.
signal_reason: Asserts no PtyBytes for the click plus the focus change and gated typing.
uniqueness_reason: Terminal-mode pane-switch suppression is a distinct boundary from Browse-mode clicks.
fidelity_reason: Real split panes with a real tracking-mode screen.
recommendation_reason: Protects against forwarding the pane-switch click.

behavior: A dashboard with no session and no acknowledged screen receives a click at 50,10 and must not emit PtyBytes(Vec::new()).
failure_caught: A click with no focused/ready session being encoded as empty or partial PTY bytes instead of staying in dashboard capture.
criticality_reason: Losing mouse capture is a bounded UI misrouting.
signal_reason: Only assert_ne against PtyBytes(Vec::new()) passes for almost any action, including non-empty PtyBytes or Detach, so most wrong outcomes escape.
uniqueness_reason: No distinct input beyond the capture tests; the named Terminal-mode boundary is not constructed.
fidelity_reason: The fixture never enters Terminal mode (it has no session), so the claimed state is replaced by a Browse-mode click on an empty dashboard.
recommendation_reason: Strengthen to assert Redraw/None and mouse_capture_required with a real unready session in Terminal mode; the current inequality accepts non-empty PTY bytes and Detach.

behavior: A press on the sidebar border column beside the pane starts a sidebar resize (Redraw and then release Redraw), while a press one row above the pane returns None.
failure_caught: Clamping an out-of-pane press to the nearest pane cell and sending a phantom click to the application at coordinates the user did not target.
criticality_reason: A clamped press injects a wrong-coordinate click; bounded to the pane interaction.
signal_reason: Exact action assertions for the border press, its release, and the above-pane press.
uniqueness_reason: Out-of-rectangle press classification is a distinct boundary from drag-release tests.
fidelity_reason: Real sidebar geometry, resize gesture and mouse dispatch.
recommendation_reason: Protects no-clamping at the pane boundary.

behavior: After forwarding a tracked press at (3,4), dragging one column left of the pane emits an Up at the last valid cell (3,4) with the release suffix.
failure_caught: A drag leaving the pane leaving the application's button logically held down, so its next events are misread as a drag.
criticality_reason: A stuck button degrades one program interaction; bounded with a workaround.
signal_reason: Exact press bytes then exact synthetic release bytes at the last valid cell.
uniqueness_reason: The out-of-rectangle release path is shared with the sidebar-drag case but differing destination; this is the canonical case.
fidelity_reason: Real tracking-mode screen and production held-gesture bookkeeping.
recommendation_reason: Canonical synthetic-release protection.

behavior: After forwarding a tracked press, a drag into the sidebar region emits the same synthetic Up at the last valid cell (3,4).
failure_caught: A drag into the sidebar leaving the tracked button held in the application.
criticality_reason: A stuck button degrades one program interaction; bounded.
signal_reason: Exact press and release bytes, but identical in form to the out-of-rectangle release test.
uniqueness_reason: Same release_held_leaving_rectangle path with the same expected bytes; only the drag destination differs (sidebar column instead of one column left).
fidelity_reason: Real tracking-mode screen and production gesture state.
recommendation_reason: Preservation evidence: same release_held_leaving_rectangle production path (state.rs:3460-3560), identical expected press/release bytes, and the retained representative is named by full test_id nextest|Test|ovrcr%3A%3Atui|mouse%3A%3Aleaving_the_rectangle_releases_at_last_valid_cell|default in overlap_test_ids; keep one representative and preserve the sidebar drag fixture as a case there.

behavior: After a tracked press, Ctrl-g returns EnterBrowse, the following Up returns None (not forwarded) and the next key does not type into the PTY.
failure_caught: Ctrl-g switching modes while the child still owes a release, so its next events or keys are delivered to the wrong owner.
criticality_reason: Wrong-owner input after a mode switch is bounded but can corrupt one program interaction.
signal_reason: Negative assertion on the Up and on post-switch typing, after a real forwarded press.
uniqueness_reason: Mode-switch release ordering is distinct from geometry-based release tests.
fidelity_reason: Real Dashboard mode transition and held-gesture state.
recommendation_reason: Protects release-before-switch ordering on Ctrl-g.

behavior: A press is forwarded, then pane output disables mouse tracking; the matching Up is not forwarded.
failure_caught: A held gesture encoded under the old protocol after the program changed modes, sending a stale release in the wrong encoding.
criticality_reason: A stale release in the wrong encoding is a bounded interaction defect.
signal_reason: Asserts the negative forwarding after a real protocol change through pane output.
uniqueness_reason: Protocol-change invalidation is a distinct trigger from focus/pause invalidation.
fidelity_reason: Real pane parser output, reconcile path and held gesture state.
recommendation_reason: Protects held-state invalidation on protocol change.

behavior: Wheel-up over a pane with no tracking requests HistoryBegin, and the HistoryOpened response yields a HistoryPage with start_row > 0.
failure_caught: Wheel opening History at row 0 so the user sees the oldest output instead of the tail they were watching.
criticality_reason: Opening at the wrong history position is a bounded usability failure.
signal_reason: Asserts the request type and a non-zero start row after the opened response.
uniqueness_reason: Tail-open on wheel is distinct from the three-row wheel scrolling test.
fidelity_reason: Real Dashboard wheel dispatch and real page request composition.
recommendation_reason: Protects wheel-opens-at-tail.

behavior: A wheel-down while History sits at the newest row leaves History and emits only HistoryEnd/HistoryPage messages.
failure_caught: Wheel-down at the tail leaving the session in frozen History (or sending PTY input) instead of returning to live output.
criticality_reason: A stuck frozen view is a bounded usability failure.
signal_reason: Accepts either EnterBrowse or Redraw and any mix of HistoryEnd/HistoryPage, so several stuck-state outcomes still pass.
uniqueness_reason: Return-to-live on wheel-down is distinct from wheel-open and wheel-step tests.
fidelity_reason: Real History state, response fixture and request composition.
recommendation_reason: Useful transition check, but the permissive action/request assertions limit what it rejects.

behavior: With 1000h/1006h enabled, a wheel-up over the focused pane returns exactly the SGR wheel bytes for the relative cell.
failure_caught: The dashboard stealing the wheel from a program that asked for mouse reports, so the program never scrolls.
criticality_reason: Stolen wheel input is a bounded interaction defect.
signal_reason: Exact byte assertion after a real mode-enable screen.
uniqueness_reason: Wheel forwarding is a distinct routing decision from wheel-to-history when tracking is absent.
fidelity_reason: Real tracking-mode pane and production encode_mouse path.
recommendation_reason: Protects forwarding precedence over dashboard history.

behavior: Wheel-up over the unfocused split pane focuses that pane and defers the history open until the replacement view is acknowledged, then emits HistoryBegin for that same session.
failure_caught: History opening for the previously focused session (wrong ownership) or before the new pane's view is acknowledged.
criticality_reason: Opening history for the wrong session shows another agent's output under the user's pointer.
signal_reason: Asserts focus change, the single SetView, and that the deferred HistoryBegin names the wheel's session.
uniqueness_reason: The deferred wheel history open across a focus change is a distinct integration boundary.
fidelity_reason: Real split panes, ack handshake and deferred request queue; view geometry is real.
recommendation_reason: Protects wrong-session history and acknowledged-view ordering.

behavior: After a forwarded press, a paused SessionChanged event makes the matching Up return None instead of forwarding a release to the paused session.
failure_caught: Releasing a button against a session that just paused, delivering input to a non-live process.
criticality_reason: A release against a paused session is bounded misrouting.
signal_reason: Exact positive press and negative release across the lifecycle transition.
uniqueness_reason: Pause-driven gesture cancellation is a distinct trigger from focus loss and protocol change.
fidelity_reason: Real hierarchy event, mode transition and held gesture state.
recommendation_reason: Protects gesture teardown on pause.

behavior: FocusLost returns Redraw and drops drag/up/down/wheel events; FocusGained returns Redraw and a fresh press/up pair is forwarded with the new cell coordinates.
failure_caught: Mouse input reaching the child while the terminal does not have focus, or a stale held state after focus regained.
criticality_reason: Focus-window misrouting is bounded but can click an unintended cell.
signal_reason: Matrix of four dropped events plus two exact forwarded events after regain.
uniqueness_reason: Focus lifecycle gating is distinct from the other gesture-boundary tests.
fidelity_reason: Real event_action dispatch, real tracking screen and production gesture bookkeeping.
recommendation_reason: Protects focus gating and post-focus resume.

behavior: A form blocks the Ctrl-hold jump; after the form is hidden behind Browse the same gesture labels the visible Agent row [1] but not Operator chat rows; Ctrl+C clears the draft, Cmd+Backspace preserves it, Ctrl+1 selects session 4 with a SetView, and returning to Operator keeps the draft, cursor and transcript scroll.
failure_caught: Ctrl-hold jumping to the wrong session or revealing targets from a modal; Ctrl+C/Command+Backspace leaking into the PTY or destroying the draft; navigation losing the composer cursor or transcript position.
criticality_reason: Wrong-session jumping and draft loss are lost-work/wrong-ownership failures; the transcript scroll is part of the same preserved context.
signal_reason: Many exact positive/negative render and request assertions across form, Browse, jump, cancel and return phases.
uniqueness_reason: The full form-priority plus draft/cursor/scroll preservation path is unique in reviewed coverage.
fidelity_reason: Real Dashboard with real keymap, form state, jump targets and rendering; only the server side is fixtured.
recommendation_reason: Decisive composite protection of jump targets and composer preservation.

behavior: With a narrow on-demand sidebar, Ctrl+1 neither reveals the sidebar nor changes focus; after Ctrl+L the sidebar appears and the Agent gets label [1].
failure_caught: Ctrl-hold jump silently revealing an on-demand sidebar or selecting a target the user cannot see.
criticality_reason: An unexpected sidebar reveal is a bounded UI/layout failure.
signal_reason: Asserts absence of the agent row before, presence and label after the explicit Ctrl+L, plus unchanged focus both times.
uniqueness_reason: On-demand sidebar suppression is distinct from the label/column matrix.
fidelity_reason: Real Dashboard with width-dependent geometry and sidebar preference.
recommendation_reason: Protects the hidden-sidebar jump guard.

behavior: Across 120x40/100x24/80x24/60x24/60x16/59x16, visible Agent rows get [1] at or above the 60x16 Operator floor, titles/status keep fixed columns and row count, below-floor layouts show 60×16 resize guidance, suppress labels/jumps, and mouse hit-testing still selects the drawn row.
failure_caught: Labels shifting titles or rows (layout corruption), a below-floor Ctrl+digit selecting a hidden session, or mouse hit-testing a row other than the painted one.
criticality_reason: Wrong jump targets and shifted columns misattribute sessions in the shared sidebar; layout corruption affects the main navigation surface.
signal_reason: Six-size matrix with positive/negative label assertions, exact column/row-count comparisons, resize guidance, and a mouse selection check.
uniqueness_reason: The boundary-size matrix and below-floor suppression are distinct from single-size jump tests.
fidelity_reason: Real Dashboard geometry, render and mouse hit-testing at each size.
recommendation_reason: Strong boundary matrix; label/column paint code beyond the jump target computation was inferred from its invariants.

behavior: Across two themes and four sizes: submit shows Sending, Submitted+Running shows Responding inside the transcript above the composer, clock advance moves only the spinner, mouse/PageUp do not send requests, and a tracked List response completes the state without stale Responding/Sending.
failure_caught: Stale activity after a real completion, a spinner that never advances, activity drawn outside the transcript, or drawing/clicking generating requests or PTY input.
criticality_reason: Misleading activity status is a bounded workflow problem; no durable state changes.
signal_reason: Buffer-diff and line-scan assertions pin the only changing cells and the transient words, plus an empty-outbox check after draws and clicks.
uniqueness_reason: The draw-versus-clock and List-authority interaction is distinct from response-only operator tests.
fidelity_reason: Real draw_operator over real state with TestBackend; provider side is a fixture.
recommendation_reason: High-signal activity/clock invariants; the activity paint internals were not read line by line.

behavior: In ten underlying modes (Browse, Terminal, History, Copy, Tasks, Palette, Which-key, Operator, Form, Details), Ctrl-o opens Quick message, keys/paste/ctrl-chords produce no PtyBytes or Input requests, the popup shows the typed text, and Esc restores the underlying buffer exactly.
failure_caught: Overlay input leaking to the PTY or the Server in any of those modes, or dismissing the popup leaving the underlying mode altered.
criticality_reason: Any mode leaking overlay input is wrong-target input to an agent; restoring the wrong mode also loses the user's place.
signal_reason: Ten-mode matrix with exact buffer equality after close plus negative action/request assertions.
uniqueness_reason: The all-modes overlay guard is broader than the retained quick-dispatch test, which exercises the production loop rather than ten entry states.
fidelity_reason: Real Dashboard mode fixtures and render; the quick conversation path is fixtured.
recommendation_reason: Comprehensive overlay input isolation across modes.

behavior: In Terminal mode with nothing over the pane Ctrl-o encodes 0x0f to the PTY, no Quick message appears and the footer names the Ctrl-o route; after Ctrl-g the same key opens Quick message without Input requests.
failure_caught: The dashboard intercepting Ctrl-o in Terminal mode, breaking Oh My Pi/Claude Code shortcuts, or Ctrl-g followed by Ctrl-o failing to open the popup.
criticality_reason: Intercepting Ctrl-o breaks in-agent shortcuts; bounded to one key route.
signal_reason: Exact PtyBytes for the program route, render assertions for both routes, and an empty input-request check.
uniqueness_reason: The terminal-versus-dashboard routing of one key is distinct from the overlay matrix.
fidelity_reason: Real screen/mode state, real dispatch and render.
recommendation_reason: Protects the documented Ctrl-o routing exception.

behavior: Opening Operator captures project/workspace/cwd/session/run; Create is sent with the configured provider/model; paste, Ctrl+C/A/F/H/U, Alt-B and Ctrl-C repeats send nothing; Enter sends Submit with exactly the captured context and text, and changing focus afterwards does not change the emitted request.
failure_caught: Recapturing context at submit so the message is attributed to the new focus, or any Operator key/paste leaking to the PTY.
criticality_reason: Wrong submission context attributes a message and its work to the wrong session/run; wrong-target durable effect.
signal_reason: Exact equality on Create and Submit requests (including context), a pre-focus and post-focus comparison, and exhaustive no-PTY/no-Input assertions.
uniqueness_reason: Context stability across focus changes is unique; the no-PTY matrix overlaps the quick-message guard but for native submission.
fidelity_reason: Real Dashboard request composition; conversation creation/history are fixtures.
recommendation_reason: Decisive exact-request protection for native submission context.

behavior: While Operator is shown the view request has no panes; Ctrl-g and Esc each leave it, the footer returns to BROWSE, the pane view is restored focused on session 1 without moving selection, and o returns to the same draft.
failure_caught: Leaving Operator without restoring the pane view, or restoring a different focused session and losing the draft.
criticality_reason: A lost pane view or draft is lost work; a wrong focused session is wrong ownership.
signal_reason: Both exit keys are exercised with exact pane/focus assertions and a draft round-trip.
uniqueness_reason: The empty-panes-while-Operator rule plus restore-on-exit is distinct from the quick-message overlay tests.
fidelity_reason: Real Dashboard view composition, retarget and render.
recommendation_reason: Protects view restoration and draft retention; pane-emptying internals were inferred from the asserted SetView.

behavior: The form shows 'Provider: ChatGPT' (never 'chat_gpt'), Tab+Right switches to Grok, and the quick message caption reads 'ChatGPT / gpt-6.1-sol'.
failure_caught: Raw saved identifiers leaking into the UI, or the provider switch not being reflected in the caption.
criticality_reason: Cosmetic naming; the underlying provider selection still works.
signal_reason: Positive/negative substring checks for the labels and the switched state.
uniqueness_reason: Provider labels are a small distinct label contract, not otherwise asserted.
fidelity_reason: Real Dashboard render with the protocol label mapping.
recommendation_reason: Cheap label contract; low criticality but no reason to drop.

behavior: At 55x15, 80x3 and 120x24 row 0 shows 'Operator [o]' and a left click at column 9 opens the native conversation list.
failure_caught: The header label being drawn where no mouse target exists (or the target elsewhere), so Operators cannot be opened on narrow/short terminals.
criticality_reason: A dead affordance on small terminals is a bounded usability failure with keyboard workaround.
signal_reason: Render-derived text plus a real click asserting the Operator List request at three geometries.
uniqueness_reason: Header hit-target agreement across tiny screens is distinct from the general header tests.
fidelity_reason: Real geometry, render and mouse dispatch; server list is fixtured.
recommendation_reason: Protects the draw/hit-target agreement at small sizes.

behavior: With a hierarchy installed, sidebar row 1 contains 'OPERATOR'.
failure_caught: The Operator section heading missing or placed below the project rows, hiding the section boundary.
criticality_reason: Cosmetic sidebar heading placement.
signal_reason: Single positive substring assertion at 80x24.
uniqueness_reason: A small layout label distinct from the jump-label tests.
fidelity_reason: Real Dashboard render through TestBackend.
recommendation_reason: Minor but concrete heading assertion; render internals beyond the assertion were not inspected.

behavior: Two saved conversations keep independent drafts, cursors and transcript anchors across selection, scroll, resize and collapse; only one row shows the selection marker; the rendered receipt's hit row collapses the right chat; a pending submit offers no Send; and a saved-history submit uses OperatorContext::default instead of recapturing terminal context.
failure_caught: Selecting chat B carrying chat A's draft/anchor into it, a collapse click hitting another chat, a pending submit being re-offered, or a saved-history message being attributed to the current terminal context.
criticality_reason: Cross-chat draft/context mixing is lost work and wrong attribution; the context default protects a durable submission target.
signal_reason: Per-chat exact anchors, single-marker counts, render-derived hit rows and exact Submit conversation/text/context assertions.
uniqueness_reason: Independent per-conversation draft/anchor geometry and saved-history context neutrality are not evidenced elsewhere.
fidelity_reason: Real Dashboard journal state, render and Submit composition; saved history is a fixture.
recommendation_reason: High-value composite; the journal paint/hit geometry internals were not read, so some assertions are understood from outcomes.

behavior: With a 30-session project and the selected session at the tree viewport bottom, loading five Operator conversations (list growth above it) keeps the selection marker at row 16 with session 30 focused.
failure_caught: Operator section growth pushing the selected session below the visible tree so the user loses sight of the selection or the marker lands on another row.
criticality_reason: A scrolled-out selection is a bounded navigation/usability failure.
signal_reason: Exact selected-row vector and focused session after the list response, via the shared viewport fixture.
uniqueness_reason: List-growth reflow is one of three distinct transition cases (growth vs collapse/expand vs archive).
fidelity_reason: Real Dashboard viewport math and render.
recommendation_reason: Protects the growth transition with an exact selected-row assertion.

behavior: With the Operator section already loaded, two project-header clicks (collapse then expand) each keep the selected session marker at the viewport bottom.
failure_caught: Collapse/expand leaving the selection off-screen or painting the marker on a non-selected row.
criticality_reason: A mis-scrolled selection is a bounded usability failure.
signal_reason: Exact selected-row vector after each of two reflow transitions; the loop does not vary the case beyond repetition.
uniqueness_reason: Same viewport invariant as the growth case, exercised through a different transition.
fidelity_reason: Real Dashboard collapse state, viewport math and render.
recommendation_reason: Small distinct collapse/expand transition check.

behavior: Hovering and clicking the close control then Enter emits Close; the archived Closed response reclaims the conversation row and keeps the selected session marker at the viewport bottom.
failure_caught: An archived conversation's row not being reclaimed, leaving the tree offset pointing past the content or the selection invisible.
criticality_reason: A bad scroll offset after archiving is a bounded navigation failure.
signal_reason: Exact Close request, exact archived response handling, then the exact selected-row invariant.
uniqueness_reason: Archive-driven row reclamation and offset clamping is a distinct transition from growth/collapse.
fidelity_reason: Real Dashboard close flow, viewport math and render.
recommendation_reason: Protects offset clamping after archive.

behavior: Space p n opens the Create branch form (Inspect answered), then a pasted 'feature/leader-workspace' appears in the form with project consigint and a Branch name field, and no Task/Start fields.
failure_caught: n opening a terminal/agent form, or the pasted branch name not reaching the form's branch field.
criticality_reason: Opening the wrong creation form is a bounded workflow failure.
signal_reason: Negative which-key/Task/Start assertions plus positive branch/project/field assertions after a real Inspect response.
uniqueness_reason: Branch-form routing overlaps the palette search entry test but adds the menu path and value entry.
fidelity_reason: Real Dashboard palette form and render; registry is a fixture.
recommendation_reason: Protects the p n route and explicit branch name entry.

behavior: Selecting the typed Focus hint runs it (the screen acknowledges), the palette closes so z is sent to the PTY, and a late Internal Inspect error never reaches the footer.
failure_caught: A closed palette leaving its inspection request live so a late error surfaces as a phantom failure, or the palette retaining input capture.
criticality_reason: A phantom error is a bounded feedback problem; input routing itself is separately asserted.
signal_reason: Exact PtyBytes after the hint plus a negative footer assertion for the late error.
uniqueness_reason: Late-response dropping across palette close is a distinct lifecycle boundary.
fidelity_reason: Real Dashboard request ids/ignored responses and render; the hint target is a fixture screen.
recommendation_reason: Protects late Inspect error suppression.

behavior: Space shows the which-key 'w  Workspace' group; w n closes it and opens a form titled New agent session with an Agent harness field.
failure_caught: w n opening the wrong form (terminal/branch) or leaving the which-key popup over the form.
criticality_reason: Wrong form routing is a bounded workflow failure.
signal_reason: Substring assertions for the menu, popup dismissal and two form labels; no request/field-value check.
uniqueness_reason: New-agent routing overlaps the empty-workspace destination test but without a destination assertion.
fidelity_reason: Real Dashboard palette form and render; agent catalog is real detection.
recommendation_reason: Useful route smoke check; beyond the form title the created request is not asserted.

behavior: Space w t opens a Create terminal form with Start: Terminal, Workspace/Name/Command fields and no agent fields or model discovery; Alt+Enter sends CreateSession kind Terminal for consigint/auth.
failure_caught: The named Terminal route opening an agent form, starting model discovery, or creating a session in the wrong workspace/kind.
criticality_reason: Creating a session in the wrong workspace/kind places durable work in the wrong branch.
signal_reason: Exact form/field positive-negative assertions, empty-outbox check and exact CreateSession project/workspace/kind.
uniqueness_reason: The named-terminal route with Start preselected is distinct from the generic create-terminal form.
fidelity_reason: Real Dashboard form construction, submit composition and render; no server process needed for the request assertion.
recommendation_reason: Strong request-level protection; the submit formatter was not read line by line.

behavior: ? opens which-key; four Down presses then Enter open the Register project form with Repository and Workspace root fields.
failure_caught: Browse selection not moving (Enter opening the first/wrong action) on the help popup.
criticality_reason: Wrong selection is a bounded navigation failure.
signal_reason: Asserts the popup then two form labels; the fixed four Downs makes it order-dependent but exact.
uniqueness_reason: Keyboard browsing of which-key is distinct from mouse hit-testing.
fidelity_reason: Real Dashboard which-key state and palette form.
recommendation_reason: Small concrete browse check.

behavior: Both leaders list t/w/p/v, Register project and Detach but no notification/sound toggles; S still sends SetSetting ready_sound; after a SettingsChanged event the palette searches show Disable ready sound / Enable desktop notifications with their Settings rows.
failure_caught: Toggles reappearing in the which-key menu, S not toggling the sound setting, or the search entries not reflecting the server setting.
criticality_reason: Menu/palette command drift is a bounded discoverability failure.
signal_reason: Positive and negative menu rows for two openers plus a real SetSetting request and state-dependent search results.
uniqueness_reason: The no-toggles menu contract plus setting-dependent search is distinct from the nested which-key group tests.
fidelity_reason: Real Dashboard keymap, which-key hints, setting request and render.
recommendation_reason: Protects the menu contract and toggle routing; entry-ranking internals were not read.

behavior: At 80x40 and 160x60 the popup is at most 48 wide and 30 high, anchored two cells from the bottom-right, and every buffer cell outside its border equals the pre-popup dashboard.
failure_caught: The popup drawing outside its area and corrupting the dashboard background, or exceeding its documented size.
criticality_reason: Overlay painting errors are cosmetic/incidental.
signal_reason: Full buffer equality outside the detected popup area across two sizes.
uniqueness_reason: Popup geometry is a small distinct contract from the popup's contents.
fidelity_reason: Real Dashboard render over a real background buffer.
recommendation_reason: Exact non-overdraw check.

behavior: At 80x40, 40x16, 20x12 and 20x8, after 40 scroll-down ticks the terminal cursor sits on q and a click on that cursor cell returns Detach.
failure_caught: Hit-testing a scrolled last row against its unscrolled position, so a click runs a different action (or the bottom row is unreachable).
criticality_reason: A wrong-row action can detach the dashboard; bounded with a restart workaround.
signal_reason: Render-derived cursor coordinates plus exact action at four sizes, after real scroll events.
uniqueness_reason: Scrolled hit-testing after resize is distinct from the unscrolled rendered-row click test.
fidelity_reason: Real which-key layout, scroll state, cursor paint and mouse hit-testing.
recommendation_reason: Protects scroll/resize hit-testing agreement.

behavior: At 80 columns the Create branch row omits its description, the detail line below carries it and the project, the description reaches the last inner line, Backspace returns to the group, and a disabled Enter Focus row is DIM with the 'waiting for acknowledged screen' reason.
failure_caught: Narrow popups clipping descriptions or hiding why an action is disabled, so the user cannot tell what a row does or why it fails.
criticality_reason: Clipped help text is a bounded discoverability failure.
signal_reason: Row/detail positional assertions, the last-inner-line check, and the DIM-style plus reason assertion for the disabled row.
uniqueness_reason: Narrow-layout description carriage and disabled-reason rendering are distinct from popup geometry.
fidelity_reason: Real Dashboard which-key render and key handling.
recommendation_reason: Protects narrow popup text placement and disabled reason.

behavior: A bare Dashboard shows 'Welcome to OVRCR', the numbered register/create hints and the Space/:/? legend, and omits Home:/Socket: instance paths.
failure_caught: An empty instance rendering a blank or misleading screen, or leaking instance paths into the start screen.
criticality_reason: A missing first-run screen is a bounded onboarding failure.
signal_reason: Four positive and two negative substring checks on the real empty render.
uniqueness_reason: The start-screen content is a distinct state not covered by other palette tests.
fidelity_reason: Real Dashboard render through TestBackend.
recommendation_reason: Concrete empty-state check; the start-screen paint internals were not inspected.

behavior: Searching 'create branch' lists 'Create branch (w)' and no Task entry.
failure_caught: Search ranking/filtering dropping the branch entry for its own words, or surfacing an unrelated Task row.
criticality_reason: A missing palette entry is a bounded discoverability failure.
signal_reason: Two substring assertions; it catches the named regression but no ranking or boundary detail.
uniqueness_reason: The same entry is already reached and asserted by the Space p n branch-form test.
fidelity_reason: Real Dashboard palette search and render.
recommendation_reason: Cheap search smoke check; kept as a direct entry-point assertion.

behavior: At 80 and 320 columns, the rendered 'a  Register project' row's cell column is clicked and opens the register form while focus stays on session 1; clicking outside the popup at 0,10 neither acts nor dismisses which-key.
failure_caught: Mouse hit-testing against a different row than the painted one (byte-vs-cell offsets), or background clicks acting under the overlay.
criticality_reason: Wrong-row actions are bounded but can trigger destructive commands.
signal_reason: Render-derived cell coordinates at two widths plus exact form/focus/negative-popup assertions.
uniqueness_reason: Rendered-row mouse agreement plus background blocking is distinct from the scrolled-row test.
fidelity_reason: Real which-key layout, mouse hit-testing and palette form.
recommendation_reason: Protects drawn-row hit-testing and background blocking.

behavior: For palette, which-key and tasks, opening the overlay during a divider drag means the later Up does not resize panes; after dismissal a pane click is Redraw and a drag is None, still with two panes; a terminal right-click held then a toolbar click releases the button (Input) before Inspect opens Commands.
failure_caught: Divider drag ownership surviving a keyboard overlay, so a later click resizes panes unexpectedly, or an overlay opening while a tracked button stays held.
criticality_reason: Stuck gesture ownership corrupts layout and can send a stray release/input to a pane; bounded by re-dragging the divider.
signal_reason: Three-overlay loop with exact post-dismissal action assertions, plus byte-order and pane-count checks in the terminal case.
uniqueness_reason: The overlay-versus-divider-gesture arbitration is distinct from the which-key mouse tests.
fidelity_reason: Real Dashboard split geometry, gesture state, overlay capture and request order.
recommendation_reason: Protects gesture ownership handoff across overlays.

behavior: PageUp leaves a pending HistoryBegin; t opens the tasks overlay and a late HistoryOpened response does not replace it.
failure_caught: A cancellable history begin still applying its opened response, so the tasks overlay is replaced (or History opens) after the user moved on.
criticality_reason: A stolen overlay is a bounded UI failure.
signal_reason: Positive tasks render before and after the late response; the history begin cancellation is the asserted transition.
uniqueness_reason: History-begin cancellation by a hotkey is distinct from overlay cancellation of mouse drags.
fidelity_reason: Real Dashboard pending request, cancellation and render.
recommendation_reason: Protects late HistoryOpened suppression.

behavior: Paste and key releases under which-key return None and never reach the PTY; Esc closes it, after which z is typed; a second open with t r keeps the popup, Esc returns BROWSE, and after Space t Enter the '?' and ' ' keys are typed to the program.
failure_caught: Overlay input leaking to the child while the popup is open, or closing which-key leaving input revoked/broken.
criticality_reason: Leaking overlay keys into an agent is wrong-target input.
signal_reason: Exact None assertions for paste/release, then positive PtyBytes for ordinary keys after close, plus footer state.
uniqueness_reason: Readiness/input-release after overlay dismissal is distinct from the buffer-restore quick-message test.
fidelity_reason: Real Dashboard dispatch, readiness and render.
recommendation_reason: Protects overlay input isolation and post-close typing.

behavior: In Copy mode Space opens a popup containing the Selection group; v sets the anchor and closes the popup while the single pane stays captured; ? then Esc stays in Copy; Ctrl-g from the leader runs the listed Browse action and the footer returns BROWSE.
failure_caught: Space in Copy mode replacing the capture keymap with the Browse keymap, v not anchoring, or leader Ctrl-g not executing its action.
criticality_reason: A broken copy leader blocks one editing workflow; bounded.
signal_reason: Positive Selection-group and pane-count assertions plus negative popup checks and footer state after each transition.
uniqueness_reason: The Copy-mode leadership semantics are distinct from Browse which-key tests.
fidelity_reason: Real which-key hints, Copy state and render.
recommendation_reason: Protects capture preservation and anchor/leader semantics.

behavior: In Copy mode with ? open, the terminal cursor sits at the popup's first motion row and that cell is h.
failure_caught: The cursor left in the underlying copy pane so keyboard browsing is invisible/misdirected.

signal_reason: Exact Position and cell-symbol assertions from the real render.

recommendation_reason: Exact small cursor contract.

behavior: Clicking an empty workspace card clears the focused session and shows 'spacelift-agent / empty' with 'n new agent session'; n emits read-only Inspect+List, and after both responses the New agent session form carries the clicked destination.
failure_caught: The new-agent form capturing the previously selected workspace/session, so a session is created in the wrong branch (wrong ownership).
criticality_reason: A wrong creation destination places durable work in the wrong branch/worktree.
signal_reason: Render-derived card click, exact request set (Inspect+List only) and destination text on the resulting form.
uniqueness_reason: Click-to-destination selection for an empty workspace is distinct from the n-from-menu/forms tests.
fidelity_reason: Real Dashboard sidebar/card hit-testing, form construction and render; registry/hierarchy fixtures are read-only.
recommendation_reason: Protects the clicked destination; sidebar hit-testing internals were inferred from the successful click.
